summary: Broker drops the socket: the manager reconnects, sends connect again, waits for ck and subscribes the touchline and the depth feed again; an update before the new acknowledgement carries only what this connection sent, then the acknowledgement and an update come through.

notes: The desktop clears its snapshots on every connect (streaming.rs on_connected); the web keeps them across a reconnect (_on_close / _resubscribe_all clear nothing), which shows when an update comes before the new acknowledgement.

No frame carries the depth feed's `ltt` (an IST HH:MM:SS): the desktop reads it on the IST day the tick arrives (streaming.rs clock_on_day_of), so its epoch-ms value depends on the day the case runs and cannot be pinned here; brokers::definedge::tests::quote_feed::a_depth_message_carries_the_full_quote_and_the_trade_time pins it. Without it both sides take the feed time `ft` (epoch seconds) as the trade time.

deviations.reason: The web forwards Definedge's raw time as ltt: the feed time `ft` in epoch seconds (or the depth feed's clock text HH:MM:SS), a wrong value where feed timestamps are epoch milliseconds (docs/prompt/websockets-format.md); it is a JSON string as well. The desktop sends the epoch ms value.

The web keeps the snapshot of the connection that dropped (_on_close and _resubscribe_all clear nothing) and publishes its average price as current with the first update after a reconnect; the desktop starts each connection's snapshot afresh (a cached market field belongs to the session that sent it). Lead decision 2026-11-09: restarting the merge after a reconnect is a desktop improvement, a web defect.
